newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mixed in light activity.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mixed in light activity.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed on Monday, with the money market yield curve steepening, as a lack of significant news or data helped to keep activity very light, dealers said.

"There's fairly light flows. There's not a lot of numbers coming out this week. It's a bit light on data," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "It's opened up pretty much where it closed (Friday)."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.85 percent from 2.86 percent at the close of trading on Friday.
Canadian data on international security transactions out this morning had little impact on the money market, dealers said.

"I don't think anyone has a great interest in going really long any particular issue but then again no one has really any great interest in shorting anything either. The lack of supply is going to keep us in relatively well," said a second T-bill dealer, also with a bank-owned brokerage.
The second dealer said international accounts appeared to be waiting for a backup in yields before they were willing to enter the market.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.16 percent from 3.15 percent. The one-year T-bill softened to yield 3.63 percent from 3.60 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 2.95-3.0 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
